source._source_note: GPL-3.0 ERPNext app (v16.53.0, the newest v16 GA release at the retarget, 2026-11-01) on the MIT Frappe framework v16.53.0. Built via frappe_docker's bench toolchain (bench init --frappe-branch v16.53.0 + bench get-app erpnext v16.53.0 + implicit bench build); the vendor stage checks both clones resolve to the pinned commits. Hand-kit forks frappe_docker's production Containerfile (product-kits/erpnext/build/Dockerfile.vendor -> vendored tarballs -> Dockerfile.offline.pinned hermetic reassembly). ERPNext uses the standard Frappe desk UI (server-rendered assets in sites/assets via nginx) — NOT a separate Vue SPA like frappecrm.
source.source_date_epoch_provenance: the time release v16.53.0-CE-ubuntu24.04-r4 was cut (2026-11-23T04:32:30Z), by scripts/rerelease-agenda.py: ReadyStack dates an image by when its release was packaged (owner 2026-11-10), recorded here once and used by every rebuild of the release; it builds upstream commit 9cd11b19575b, dated 2026-10-28T20:44:02Z (source.commit_epoch).

python_runtime._note: CPython 3.14.10 compiled from python.org's release tarball (sha256 from python.org's release API, scripts/cpython-pin.py) plus upstream's own fix commit 7d9da92 for CVE-2026-119170 (gh-160923, PR #160984, on CPython's 3.14 branch since 2026-11-06; a hashlib regression in 3.14.10 only, under an OpenSSL in FIPS mode; python.org has not yet released a 3.14.11), applied unmodified with `patch -p1` to the extracted source before configure (python_runtime.patches; the hand kit's vendor stage fetches the patch file, pinned by sha256, it ships in vendored/erpnext-src/python/ beside the tarball, and the offline build checks and applies it again, so a customer's rebuild carries it; drop the patch when the pin moves to a release that contains it), against Ubuntu 24.04's own libraries -- libssl3t64, libsqlite3-0, zlib1g, libexpat1, libffi8, liblzma5, libbz2-1.0, libuuid1, libzstd1, libncursesw6, libreadline8t64 -- which Ubuntu's security team maintains, the scan sees as debs, and apt upgrades fix (owner decision 2026-10-10, after python-build-standalone 20261009 was found to bundle SQLite 3.53.1 with two HIGH CVEs fixed upstream four months earlier). The vendor stage only fetches the tarball and the build toolchain's debs; the compile runs in the offline (--network=none) build, reproducibly (gen_dockerfile.cpython_build_cmd: SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, no PGO/LTO, fixed --build triple and source path, stripped, checked-hash .pyc). Never built: _dbm, _gdbm, _tkinter (no Berkeley DB, GDBM or Tk); no test suite, idle, tkinter, turtledemo or static libpython in the image. mpdecimal is the copy in CPython's own source (noble has no libmpdec). Move the pin with scripts/cpython-pin.py --write for each CPython patch release.

patches.name: cpython-3.14.10-7d9da92-fips-hashlib.diff
patches.why: CVE-2026-119170 is a hashlib FIPS-property regression in CPython 3.14.10 only; python.org has released no 3.14.11, so the fix is taken as upstream's own commit 7d9da92 from the 3.14 branch (gh-160923 / PR #160984, 2026-11-06), applied unmodified before configure. Owner policy 2026-11-17: apply upstream's exact fix commit ourselves rather than wait, and never hand-write a fix. The sha256 is of the commit's .diff as GitHub serves it (read 2026-11-17 for homeassistant; downloaded again and re-hashed 2026-11-23).

node_dist._note: The official nodejs.org build node-v24.22.2-linux-x64.tar.gz (latest 24.x on 2026-10-29; Frappe v16.53.0 package.json engines.node >=24; 24.22.1 of 2026-10-20 is the Node.js security release that fixes CVE-2026-111497 in the Brotli copy Node compiles in, Bitnami BIT-node-2026-111497: affected before 24.22.1). sha256 copied from https://nodejs.org/dist/v24.22.2/SHASUMS256.txt.asc, whose signature verified as a Good signature from Node.js release key 5BE8A3F6C8A5C01D106C0AD820B1A390B168D356 (Antoine du Hamel, listed in nodejs/release-keys) on 2026-10-29; the same pin as product-kits/erpnext/build/Dockerfile.vendor's NODE_VERSION/NODE_SHA256 (bump both together).

source._framework_note: Frappe is pinned to its release TAG (Dockerfile.vendor ARG FRAPPE_BRANCH and FRAPPE_COMMIT; v16.53.0 in this release, see the top-level _framework_note), not the floating version-16 branch, so the framework version inside the image is known and stated (audit 2026-09-25).
source._weasyprint_note: WeasyPrint 70.x replaces Frappe v16.51.0's exact pin WeasyPrint==68.0 (Dockerfile.vendor venv upgrade step): GHSA-r543-q48m-4c9j (HIGH; EPS images reach Ghostscript) is fixed only in 70.0, Frappe v16 deprecates WeasyPrint (frappe/utils/weasyprint.py: 'removed in version 17') and Frappe's develop branch no longer depends on it. 70.0 declares the same requirements as 68.0 and the build asserts each one is met. Frappe calls it only for builder print formats stored on WeasyPrint: frappe.get_print(as_pdf=True) -> pdf_generator hook frappe.utils.weasyprint.get_weasyprint_pdf -> weasyprint_legacy.PrintFormatGenerator.render_pdf. Measured 2026-10-10 on the offline image (render test in a throwaway build stage on <redacted: internal host>, the image's own entrypoint and supervisord with local MariaDB and Redis): a submitted Sales Invoice on a builder format stored on WeasyPrint rendered through that path to a 1-page %PDF-1.7 of 7,860 bytes (Producer 'WeasyPrint 70.0'; the legacy generator was called once; the overlaid header present), with a Letter Head to 8,392 bytes carrying both overlays, and over HTTP (download_pdf through nginx and gunicorn) to the same 7,860 bytes (HTTP 200 application/pdf); the same layout on Typst rendered 15,568 bytes; the Standard format failed with 'OSError: No wkhtmltopdf executable found'. Frappe's own TestWeasyPrintEngine passed 15/15 on a frappe-only site.
